# Salesforce Analytics Embedding SDK — Example Apps

> Frontend reference apps for @salesforce/analytics-embedding-sdk 2.0 in
> React 19, Vanilla JavaScript, and Angular 22.

## Documentation
- Official SDK overview: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/analytics/sdk/guide/sdk-overview.html
- Salesforce prerequisites: `docs/prerequisites.md`
- Demo authentication: `docs/how-to-get-frontdoor-url.md`

## Examples
- `examples/react-vite/` — class API, hooks, browser routing, lazy Agent route
- `examples/vanilla-js/` — one HTML document, CDN module, custom-element API, hash views
- `examples/angular/` — class API, standalone components, signals, lazy routing
- `tools/frontdoor-url/` — local Node OAuth Web Server Flow + PKCE + UI Bridge utility

## Authentication
- The local utility can generate a fresh frontdoor URL for configured sandbox/test orgs.
- The setup forms accept that URL for local demos.
- Credentials stay in JavaScript memory only; reload/reset discards them.
- The repository never instructs users to copy a browser session cookie.
- Production integrations use a trusted backend, OAuth 2.0 Web Server Flow, and Salesforce UI Bridge.

## SDK surface demonstrated
- `initializeAnalyticsSdk`
- `Status.SUCCESS` and failure handling
- `OrgStates.AUTH_REDIRECT`
- `retryOrAddOrgs`, including inspection of its response
- `AnalyticsDashboard`, `AnalyticsMetric`, `AnalyticsVisualization`, `AnalyticsAgent`
- `EventName.ERROR` and `EventName.COMPONENT_LOADED`
- lifecycle cleanup for SDK-backed elements

## Consistency
- `orgUrl` validation checks HTTPS syntax; the SDK/org validates the actual host.
- The setup form accepts IDs or API names for dashboards, metrics, visualizations, and Analytics Agents; at least one is required.
- Error concepts are consistent across all three examples.
